description: Issue #838 AC5, the profile-blind half. `ol-duplicate-definition` is not gated on any profile: `spec/execution-model.md:82-88` makes phase-1 registration unconditional ("The reader registers every `define`/`to` procedure **and every `struct` declaration** … a name an earlier declaration in the program or an imported module already registered raises `ol-duplicate-definition`"), and `spec/data-structures.md:304` says the same of a struct type name. Note the profile set here is **`core-language` alone, with `data` absent**, while every `struct` below still participates. That is the whole point: a profile decides whether a name *works*, never whether a program may declare it (`spec/grammar.md:408`), and `@openlogo/runtime`'s own phase-1 guard is profile-blind, so a checker gated on `data` would make `check()` and `execute()` disagree — the disagreement `docs/design-notes/0007-binding-vs-registration.md` says this ruling removes. Its sibling `declare-built-in-names-core-only` is the same guard for `ol-reserved-word`. What the program pins, line by line: line 2 is a struct duplicating a struct (original line 1); line 6 is a struct duplicating a define (original line 3); and line 7 is a define duplicating that SAME line-3 define, with a struct declaration sitting between them. That third row is a third declaration of one name across mixed kinds, so its original_span must be line 3 and NOT line 6. This is a check-mode fixture: nothing is executed and no events are produced.
